$comment: The initial-route bundle budget: the gzipped size of the entry JS the browser must download before the first route paints. A ONE-WAY RATCHET — raising max_gzip_bytes requires a CODEOWNERS review (this file is listed in .github/CODEOWNERS), which is what turns a size regression into a decision instead of a drift. `make budget-bundle` measures web/dist and fails if it exceeds max_gzip_bytes; the measured number is printed into the CI summary.
$derivation: MEASURED, not chosen. 256000 was an unmeasured placeholder; verify-before-phase-0 V13 requires the number come from a real build of the empty shell — React 19 + Router + Query + @tanstack/react-virtual plus one 12-column virtualised table. That shell measures 98695 bytes gzipped, so the budget is 128000: ~30% headroom over the measurement, and less than half the 250 KB design ceiling in .claude/rules/web.md. For scale, the same build without the /_design fixture and the virtual list is 86895 bytes, so the design-system vocabulary and TanStack Virtual together cost 11800 bytes gzipped.
$headroom_rationale: 30% is enough for the Phase 3 message catalogue, the self-hosted Phosphor subset and ordinary shell growth without a CODEOWNERS round-trip per PR. It is NOT enough to absorb 55 eagerly-imported screens, and that is the point: the initial route is code-first and every route added to router.tsx lands in this chunk, so Phase 3 hits this ceiling and reaches for route-level code splitting instead of quietly filling 250 KB. V13: 'if the empty shell already exceeds 250 KB, decide in Phase 0 whether the answer is a different router, route-level code splitting, or an honestly larger budget.' It does not, so the answer is a real budget.
$why_the_fixture_is_eager: /_design is imported statically by web/src/router.tsx, which puts the whole token layer, every base component class and the virtualised table inside the measured entry closure. That is deliberate: it is what makes this gate keep measuring the V13 shell on every PR rather than a shell that has quietly shrunk below the number the budget was derived from. Lazy-loading that route means re-deriving this number in the same change.
